title: Register and use passkeys through the native authenticator
goal: Broker server-issued WebAuthn JSON through the native device ceremony while retaining server-side account verification.

runtime.name: .NET
runtime.reason: Canonical current target; RC authoring is not GA execution.

packageAssets: Actual net11.0-windows10.0.19041 assets; neutral/reference compilation does not execute an authenticator.

workloads.name: maui-windows (native host)
workloads.reason: Matching native workload required for the application host; unavailable here. The Windows adapter alone compiles without UseMaui.

providers: Application-owned WebAuthn relying-party server and OS authenticator
platforms: Windows 10 1903+ WebAuthn and Windows Hello or a compatible FIDO2 key; Android 14+, iOS 16+, Mac Catalyst effective .NET 11 floor 17 require their native integrations
renderingModes: Native host; no Blazor rendering-mode claim
prerequisites: Existing native app host; initiate from a user action. Active Windows UI window on its UI thread, HTTPS RP identity, server-generated one-use challenge, exact native origin allowlist; domain/signing prerequisites for Apple/Android.
constraints: .NET 10 is comparison only; no older-target applicability route or ninth foundation. Treat returned JSON as untrusted. Verify challenge, RP ID, origin, attestation/assertion and account policy on the server before issuing a session. IsSupported is not ceremony proof.
stabilityLimitations: Stable public contract inspected in RC2; no GA execution claim.

selectionNotes: .NET 10 is comparison only; no older-target applicability route or ninth foundation. Treat returned JSON as untrusted. Verify challenge, RP ID, origin, attestation/assertion and account policy on the server before issuing a session. IsSupported is not ceremony proof.

evidence.scope: Actual Windows contract compilation; no native host or ceremony execution.

humanProof.scope: Windows adapter compiled; native host build failed NETSDK1147 (maui-tizen). Native ceremony/server interoperability not-tested under PIN-699. PIN-936 remains open and has not executed; unavailable native actions are excluded, not promised for later.
